text:
Maria (product): Hey team — sharing RFC draft for API key tenant/project mapping and scoped keys: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/tenant-mapping-draft. Need review on requirements, acceptance criteria, and a migration plan. Goal: support per-org API keys that can be scoped to one or more projects and model-groups while remaining backward compatible with current flat keys.

Sam (eng-security): Thanks. Quick high-level Qs: 1) token format — opaque vs JWT? 2) where do we persist scope metadata (KVS next to key vs separate table)? 3) enforcement: gateway-level early reject or service-level check?

Maria (product): Prefers opaque for rotation simplicity, but open to embedding minimal claims to avoid DB hit on every token. Product asks: must be easy for customers to create project-scoped keys and to rotate without downtime.

Julian (eng-platform): If we go opaque + DB lookup, caching TTL matters. Suggests a hybrid: short-lived cache (200ms-2s) + local LRU per node. Also need to index by org_id + key_id for quick lookups — anticipating rate-limited hot keys.

Tara (infra): HSM/KMS integration is required for key material; we should never log raw key. Audit logs must record key_id, org_id, actor, and operation. Rotation automation should support staged rollouts (old key -> dual-accept -> revoke).

Sam (eng-security): Proposed enforcement model: gateway authenticates key_id, fetches metadata (org, projects, allowed_models), enforces scope at gateway for routing decisions (fast path). Downstream services should also check for model-level allow-listing for critical operations. Edge-case: traffic between internal services that use service tokens — ensure tenant isolation enforced end-to-end.

Eli (customer-sig): Customer ask: can one key be scoped to multiple projects in an org? Yes/no? Also request for read-only scoped keys for embeddings pipelines so SRE can create keys without write perms.

Maria (product): Yes to multi-project keys. Need explicit role scopes (read, write, admin) attached to keys. Add acceptance criteria for role-based scopes.

Sam (eng-security): Draft acceptance criteria (please comment):
- AC-1: New API keys can be created with fields: org_id, project_ids (list), roles (list), allowed_models (optional list), expiry (optional).
- AC-2: Gateway rejects any request where the key_id exists but the requested project/model is outside project_ids/allowed_models.
- AC-3: Existing flat API keys should keep working for 6 months; they map to org-wide admin-equivalent scopes by default unless migrated.
- AC-4: Rotation: new key can be created and toggled into dual-accept mode for up to 1 week. Revoke triggers immediate deny.
- AC-5: Audit logs must surface key_id, org_id, project_id, actor_id, and action for every authentication/authorization decision.

Julian (eng-platform): Also add perf SLOs: auth path must add <5ms median latency for cached keys, <20ms p99 with DB lookup under normal load. Need load test scenarios.

Tara (infra): Edge cases we should capture:
- EC-1: Deleted project: keys referencing deleted project should be treated as invalid for that project but still valid for other projects.
- EC-2: Org transfer: when a project is moved between orgs, keys must not implicitly gain access — require explicit migration.
- EC-3: Stale cache during rotation: dual-accept window must be explicit so in-flight requests are allowed.
- EC-4: Cross-tenant exports: any export calls must require explicit export permission and must be throttled/audited.

Eli (customer-sig): Migration concerns: customers with many API keys (1000s) want a bulk import/migrate tool plus CLI flag to batch-assign project scopes. Also want a preview mode to show what access would change.

Maria (product): Good call — add migration tool to deliverables. Proposed launch criteria:
- LC-1: RFC merged and API design reviewed.
- LC-2: Gateway + auth-service implementation passes integration tests (auth + routing).
- LC-3: Migration tool (preview + apply) available and tested on staging with a sample 10k-keys dataset.
- LC-4: Docs + SDK changes (node/python) shipped with migration examples.
- LC-5: Security review + threat modeling completed and KMS integration in place.

Sam (eng-security): Implementation notes: store metadata in a dedicated table keyed by key_id with columns: org_id, project_ids (jsonb), roles (jsonb), allowed_models (jsonb), created_by, created_at, status. Only store a hash of secret in DB. Add a TTL-index for expiry.

Julian (eng-platform): We also need a fallback for legacy keys: map to a synthetic key_id row at auth startup to avoid special-casing in code. Migration plan should slowly replace legacy keys with scoped rows.

Tara (infra): Observability: add a new dashboard for key usage by org/project, rows for denied requests due to scope violations. Alert if denied-scope rate spikes > 0.1% of traffic for a given org.

Sam (eng-security): Quick sample header + metadata example to discuss format:
```
Authorization: ApiKey k_live_abc123
X-Org-ID: org_789   # optional header, prefer using key metadata
```
Key metadata (example): `key_id: k_live_abc123`, `org_id: org_789`, `project_ids: [proj_a, proj_b]`, `roles: ["read","embed"]`, `allowed_models: ["redwood-3b","open-7b"]`

Maria (product): UX asks: Admins must be able to create both org-wide keys and project-limited keys in console and via API. Need clear UI for scope selection and migration helper that suggests conservative scopes.

Eli (customer-sig): Also request: ability to create ephemeral scoped keys for partners (TTL 24h) and ability to mark keys as "non-export" to block data export endpoints.

Sam (eng-security): Added to ACs: ephemeral key TTL support and non-export flag enforcement.

Julian (eng-platform): Who owns rollout? Proposed owners: Sam -> auth schema and gateway changes; Julian -> caching and perf; Tara -> KMS + rotation automation; Maria -> migration + docs; Eli -> customer validation.

DeployBot: Integration test run started for branch feature/tenant-keying — build 4821 — https://ci.redwood/4821 (status: running) :construction:

Maria (product): Next steps: please add inline comments directly on the RFC doc by EOD Wed. If no major objections, we'll schedule a design review Thurs.

Sam (eng-security): Will add detailed threat model and draft enforcement pseudocode tonight.

Julian (eng-platform): I'll prototype LRU cache and run perf numbers on staging by Friday.

Tara (infra): I'll slot KMS integration changes in next infra sprint and add audit schema.

Eli (customer-sig): I'll gather 3 customers to validate migration UX and share feedback next week.

Maria (product): :thumbsup: Thanks all — this is a good start.
